subject.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle

question: Should yielded isolated-cron handoff become a new public and persisted `deferred` run status across Gateway, CLI, hooks, Plugin SDK, and UI, or remain an internal waiting state until a final `ok`/`error` outcome exists?
rationale: Both models can fix premature completion, but they create different long-term API, persistence, CLI-exit, scheduling, and upgrade contracts; repository evidence cannot establish that permanent product choice without owner intent.

options.title: Approve `deferred` with gates
options.body: Accept the new public status only after a clean rebase, compatibility and migration proof, final-settlement semantics, and exact-head cron plus Discord evidence are complete.

options.title: Keep waiting internal
options.body: Represent the handoff as active task/progress state and persist only the eventual final cron outcome, avoiding a new public terminal-status value.

options.title: Narrow the patch
options.body: Land the shared classifier and descendant wake fix first, then handle cron status and Discord presentation in separately owned changes.

recommendation.title: Approve `deferred` with gates
recommendation.body: Accept the new public status only after a clean rebase, compatibility and migration proof, final-settlement semantics, and exact-head cron plus Discord evidence are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available feature-history candidate for the yielded subagent lifecycle that the public cron contract builds upon.
